points: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop, halting departures at all U.S. airports, after a communications problem hit all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.
The FAA called it a temporary telecommunications outage. Its cause has not been confirmed; an Alaska Airlines internal message cited communications and radar problems.
DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there is no current reason to suspect a national security threat, but did not rule out any cause, including a cyberattack.
No timeframe for resuming flights had been given. American expected disruptions for the rest of the day; United said airborne flights would continue.
The last nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, after the NOTAM pilot-alert system failed.
